incident-bot: INCIDENT: High error/latency signal on kv-cache+batching (service: inference-pool-3). Alerting on-call.

omar (oncall): jumping in. I see a spike in 5xx and p99 latency on the structured-output routes.

ashley (eng-runtime): confirming. Traces show a ton of tiny batches (batch_size=1) and concurrent KV cache churn. Looks correlated to requests that use tool/function calling with large JSON arrays in the structured output.

lina (eng-sre): exact metrics: cache_miss_rate up from 0.12 -> 0.78 in 5m; average batch_size down from 6 -> 1.8; token-cost per request spiked x8.

ashley (eng-runtime): snippet from the runtime logs:

```
[2024-04-05T20:14:22Z] kv_cache: PUT key=funcall:resp:... size=96KB
[2024-04-05T20:14:23Z] batcher: flush reason=immediate_single (frag)
[2024-04-05T20:14:23Z] runtime: model=redwood-v2 quantized seq_len=1024 request_id=... latency=673ms
[2024-04-05T20:14:24Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.82 active_entries=1.2M
```

ashley (eng-runtime): those funcalls are returning big JSON arrays (customers requesting structured 'events' arrays). Each element is being hashed into cache prefixes and invalidates prefix coalescing -> batcher can't combine requests, KV index explodes.

kevin (prod): which customers impacted? we need a customer-impact blurb for support.

maria (support): I'm seeing 3 high-priority tickets referencing huge token bills / timeouts from Enterprise accounts: #2345, #2347, #2351. Reported symptom: generation times 2-10s, occasional 502s.

omar (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle tool/funcall endpoints 2) disable KV caching for funcall responses 3) apply short-term batcher config to prefer aggregation over immediate flush.

lina (eng-sre): I can push a hotpatch. Suggest the following commands (hot path):

```
# disable kv cache for funcall responses on pool-3
redwoodctl config set /pools/pool-3/routes/funcall kv_cache.enabled=false --session=hotfix-1723

# small tweak to batcher to avoid single-request flush on structured outputs
redwoodctl config set /pools/pool-3/batcher flush_on_schema_change=false --session=hotfix-1723

# rate limit tool calls at the ingress layer
kong-plugin rate-limit add --route /v1/funcall --limit 30/s
```

deploy-bot: rolling config changes to pool-3: session=hotfix-1723.

ashley (eng-runtime): applying `kv_cache.enabled=false` for funcall route now. Watch eviction and mem use.

[~1m later]

ashley (eng-runtime): kv cache writes for funcalls dropped ~95%. batch_size recovered to ~4 within 90s. p95 latency down from 1.2s -> 320ms. 5xx rate trending down.

maria (support): relay to customers: "We're aware of intermittent timeouts and higher latencies for structured tool responses; temporary mitigation deployed and we expect normal service within 10-15 minutes. Support team will follow up individually."

kevin (prod): good. Also create a billing protection ticket to absorb anomalous token charges for affected accounts.

omar (oncall): next steps (short):
- keep kv_cache disabled for funcall route for 2h while we evaluate
- snapshot traces and sample offending payloads
- patch runtime to avoid exploding cache entries (sanitizer + size cap)
- plan a safer rollout that transforms structured arrays into placeholders for caching

lina (eng-sre): I'm handing off to maria for continued customer comms and to ashley for the deeper fix. I need to go offline for the next handover window. @maria you have the incident.

maria (support): taking the handoff. I'll coordinate with CS and DM the customers.

ashley (eng-runtime): quick note about root cause hypothesis: funcalls that return large arrays had every array element serialized with unique keys that end up being inserted into the KV prefix index. That prevents prefix sharing; continuous batcher sees too many unique prefixes and flushes early. Code-level mitigations:
- normalize structured outputs (replace arrays with token-sized placeholders for cache key computation)
- enforce `kv_cache_max_value_size=32KB` and drop caching above that
- add a cache bypass header on toolcall responses that are marked 'streaming' or 'structured'

kevin (prod): timeline for durable fix?

ashley (eng-runtime): will prototype sanitizer + size cap today, aim for canary tomorrow, full rollout after validation (48-72h).

maria (support): customer impact note for postmortem: 3 enterprise customers, intermittent failed requests, measurable cost/latency spikes, mitigated by temporary config changes.

omar (oncall): closing actions:
- incident severity -> SEV2 (customer-affecting but partial, mitigation live)
- schedule RCA with eng-runtime + eng-sre + product for tomorrow 13:00 UTC
- owner for long-term fix: ashley (eng-runtime)

lina (eng-sre): logging summary will be pushed to the incident doc: link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1723456789 (doc created).

deploy-bot: hotpatch hotfix session=hotfix-1723 applied successfully to pool-3 at 2024-04-05T20:18:40Z :white_check_mark:

maria (support): thanks team. I'll keep the customer comms open and update the tickets.

omar (oncall): handing off monitoring to the overnight oncall at 20:30 UTC. If anyone sees re-escalation, ping @oncall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
